name: Red Flag, Green Flag Split Screen
why_it_works: Buyers in high-stakes categories are scared of picking the wrong provider, not of the price. Naming the warning signs out loud makes {{brand}} the one who protects the viewer, and every green flag quietly describes how {{brand}} already works. People save these to check against the next provider they talk to.

hook.pattern: Promise to arm the viewer against a bad {{provider_type}} before they ever meet one.
examples: Three red flags your {{provider_type}} hopes you never notice.
If your {{provider_type}} does this, walk out.
Red flag or green flag? Most people miss number two.

slides.body: A good {{provider_type}} is still there tomorrow. If the deal dies overnight, it was pressure, not advice.

craft.notes: Every red flag gets its green twin in the same frame, so the list teaches instead of just scaring. Save the pressure tactic for last because it is the one viewers have personally felt, and it hands off naturally to the brand.

do_not: Describe a red flag so specifically that it points at a real local competitor
List green flags {{brand}} does not actually practice every time
Use fear without giving the viewer a way to check for themselves
compliance: Law firms: no guarantees or predictions of case outcomes; follow your state bar's advertising rules and include any required attorney-advertising label
Med spa: no treatment results or before/after claims in the flags; any medical claim needs a licensed provider's review
Financial advisor: no performance or return promises; flags describe process, not outcomes, and follow FINRA/SEC advertising rules
Real estate: include brokerage name and license info as your state requires; no promises about sale price or timeline
